articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.titleZh: 爱比克泰德的效率系统，比任何买过的 App 都强
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 效率系统的真正过滤器不是工具，而是先问一句「这是不是我的事」。
paragraphs: 现在的生产力系统都默认你是个懒惰的烂人。你的效率差，是因为你不上心，所以解决方案就是更智能的收件箱、更丰富的标签、更全的第二大脑。结果责任全压你身上，每一条碎片都被系统放大成你必须回应的事。
爱比克泰德是个被释放的奴隶，在租来的房间里教哲学，没有 Obsidian，没有 AI 代理。他的系统从一句简单的问题开始：什么归你管？他只关注自己的判断、欲望和决定。别人的行为、观点、情绪，那些不是你的事，也不是你的猴子。
Notion、Obsidian、Todoist 这些 App 都在解决后勤问题，假设每件新来的事都重要，帮你更快地处理。爱比克泰德在前提上就不同意：邮件、通知、别人的项目，这些都是天气。你可以看天气穿衣服，但别去追踪天气。
因为捕捉一件东西，就等于把它变成你的责任。写下来就是把背景噪音变成任务，你得答应去处理它。他的过滤器是：先问「这是我的事吗？」是就进系统，不是就不记、不愧疚、不建一个「想办法处理」的项目。
现代工作就是不断模糊这条界限：收件箱是别人的输出队列，任务清单一半是别人的请求。爱比克泰德的条件更极端——他连法律地位都改变不了，唯一能管的是自己怎么选、怎么想。所以别再拿门口进来的事情数量，去算你该负担的数量。

en.thesis: The real filter of a productivity system is not the tool but asking first, 'Is this mine to manage?'
paragraphs: Productivity systems today assume you are an intellectual delinquent. Your productivity sucks because you suck, so the fix is a smarter inbox, richer tags, a fuller second brain. The burden is all on you, and every scrap gets amplified into something you owe a response to.

Epictetus was a freed slave who taught philosophy from a rented room, without Obsidian, without an AI agent. His system starts with one question: what is yours to manage? He focused only on his judgments, desires, and decisions. Other people's actions, opinions, emotions — not your circus, not your monkeys.

Apps like Notion, Obsidian, and Todoist solve logistics, assuming everything that arrives is important and helping you process it faster. Epictetus disagrees at the premise: emails, notifications, other people's projects are weather. You can dress for weather, but you don't track the weather.

Because capturing something makes it yours. Writing it down turns background noise into a task, an agreement to handle it. His filter: ask first, 'Is this mine?' If yes, it enters the system. If no, you don't capture it, don't feel bad, and don't build a project called 'deal with this somehow'.

Modern work blurs that line constantly: your inbox is someone else's output queue, your task list half other people's requests. Epictetus had it harder — he couldn't change his legal status, so his only domain was what he chose to pursue and how he interpreted things. So stop counting the number of things coming at you as the number you're responsible for.

articles.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility
articles.titleZh: 追踪一批珍本的去向：终点是亚马逊的 AI 训练设施
articles.author: Emanuel Maiberg

zh.thesis: 亚马逊正在大量购入实体书、切掉书脊扫描以获取 AI 训练数据，这一此前未被报道的运作正毁掉这些书。
paragraphs: 404 Media 在一本可能被 AI 公司收购的珍本里藏了追踪器，然后一路跟到内华达州拉斯维加斯的一个亚马逊仓库。仓库里员工的工作就是拆掉书脊再快速扫描，印刷的书就此毁掉。
这个名为 VGT3 的团队标志是一条狰狞的恐龙，嘴里还叼着一本书。亚马逊购买大量书籍用于 AI 训练数据，这个操作此前从未被报道过。
这起调查揭示了一个令人不安的事实：AI 的训练方式正悄悄消耗实体书，而公众对此几乎毫无察觉。

en.thesis: Amazon is buying huge quantities of physical books, cutting off their bindings to scan them for AI training data, a previously unreported operation that destroys the books.
paragraphs: 404 Media hid a tracking device in a rare book they suspected an AI company would buy, then followed it to an Amazon warehouse in Las Vegas, Nevada. There, employees cut off bindings to scan faster, destroying the printed book in the process.
The team there, called VGT3, has a logo of a snarling dinosaur clutching a book. Amazon buying books in bulk for AI training data is something we had not known about until now.
The investigation lays bare an unsettling reality: AI's training quietly consumes physical books, with the public left almost entirely in the dark.

articles.title: Woke 1 is dead. We’ve learned nothing.
articles.titleZh: Woke 1 已死，但我们什么都没学会
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: Woke 1 所依赖的结构条件仍然存在，反扑只是复制了同样的有害动态。
paragraphs: 关于「Woke 1 太疯狂」的讨论，我持两面态度。我同意这说法对受害者道歉不够，但如果这种含糊其辞能让人转向更好的观点，那也是好事。
我想指出的是：无论 Woke 1 是什么，它产生的结构性条件依然存在，而且远不止左派政治。没有强把关人的世界里，虚假或荒谬的想法仍能像野火一样传播，变成即时共识。
我记忆最深的不是最歇斯底里的人，而是那些明知别人在胡闹却避免说错话、也避免主动反驳的人。这种「不去当那个扫兴的人」的激励机制依然存在，意味着任何话语都可能跑偏。
不幸的是，反 Woke 的反弹没有抵制糟糕的认知实践，而是在抵制关怀弱者的价值的同时，复制了同样的有毒动态。所以，什么都没学会。

en.thesis: The structural conditions that produced Woke 1 are still with us, and the backlash is replicating the same toxic dynamics.
paragraphs: I have mixed feelings about the 'Woke 1 was crazy' discourse. I agree it's inadequate as an apology to those whose lives were upended, but if this evasive framing lets people move to better views, that's good.

My point is that whatever Woke 1 was, the structural conditions that produced it are still with us, and they go far beyond left-wing politics. In a world without strong gatekeepers, false or absurd ideas can spread like wildfire and become instant conventional wisdom.

What I remember most bitterly is not the hysterical people but those who knew others were being hysterical and carefully avoided saying false or insane things — yet also avoided actively contesting them. That incentive to not be the 'well, actually' guy is still very much with us, and it means any discourse can go off the rails.

And now the anti-woke backlash isn't resisting the bad epistemic practices of the left; it's resisting the value of caring for the weak while replicating the same toxic dynamics. So we've learned nothing.

articles.title: Things you cannot buy in America?
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 外置滚筒百叶窗在美国几乎买不到，因为与当地的房屋建造方式格格不入。
paragraphs: 欧洲很多房子的窗户外面装着厚重的滚筒百叶窗，一拉下来屋里就全黑，还能隔热。那种真正的、伸手不见五指的黑暗，大多数美国人从来没体验过。
这种百叶窗在美国几乎买不到，因为它是在建房时就嵌入墙体的。美国的房屋多用木框架、墙板和干墙，根本装不了这种结构，也没有配套的供应链支持。
这篇清单很有趣，但作者自己都怀疑其中的一些项目，比如「草屋顶」是否真的买不到。每条链接都得自己点开，这篇本身不提供可带走的东西。

en.thesis: Exterior roller shutters are nearly impossible to buy in America because they clash with the country's construction methods.
paragraphs: Many European homes have heavy roller shutters built into the window exterior, giving total blackout and better insulation. The experience of true, can't-see-your-hand darkness is something most Americans have never had.

These shutters are nearly impossible to get in the US because they are built into the house during construction. Standard American wood-frame, siding, and drywall simply can't support them, and there's no domestic supply chain to maintain them.
The list is intriguing, but the author himself doubts some items, like the 'grass roof.' Each link needs to be clicked to get the details; the piece itself offers nothing to take away.

articles.title: Ban on Chinese robots leaves U.S. startups stranded
articles.titleZh: 中国机器人禁令让美国初创公司陷入困境
articles.author: Viola Zhou

zh.thesis: 美国政府对外国机器人的全面禁令，在本土供应链尚未建立时，反而可能扼杀其试图扶持的机器人初创企业。
paragraphs: 美国联邦通信委员会上个月将「高级机器人设备」列入国家安全风险清单。新规要求，外国制造的人形机器人、四足机器人，甚至扫地机器人和割草机，要进入美国市场，必须在美国组装，且按价值计算至少 65% 的零部件要产自美国。到 2029 年，这个比例还要提高到 75%。
禁令不针对任何特定国家，但普遍认为主要针对的是中国——中国主导着机器人制造。旧政策不影响已在美国销售的产品，用于研发而非销售的进口机器人也仍被允许。但初创公司创始人看不到没有中国供应链，如何商业化生产机器人。
旧金山 CosmicBrain AI 的创始人 Anto Patrex 说：「看看苹果，都是在中国制造的。你怎能期望比 iPhone 更复杂的机器人在美国制造？」他的公司原本在中国组装首款产品，如今已在加拿大另设装配厂，但关键部件仍来自中国，这使其机器人按新规无法在美销售。
总部位于休斯顿的 Persona AI 的 Michael Perry 表示，即使在 FCC 禁令之前，美国客户就已要求机器人不含中国部件，公司已从台湾、日本、韩国和意大利采购。但满足 65% 美国制造的要求依然困难。他说：「你需要提供胡萝卜，也要有大棒。现在你只给了大棒。」
中国四十年来建立起全球最完善的电子制造业，苹果约 80% 的 iPhone 在中国组装。电动车的崛起也带动了传感器、电池、执行器（将能量转化为运动的部件）产业，这些恰是机器人所需。中国机器人因此成为最灵巧、最便宜的产品，2025 年全球近 90% 的人形机器人是中国制造。
一些美国公司欢迎禁令，认为长期能抵御中国低价竞争。Agility Robotics 和 Nori Robotics 等公司认为，禁令将促使研究人员和客户转向美国产品。但布鲁金斯学会的 Kyle Chan 认为，更渐进的方式（如逐步加征关税）更好，当前的禁令过于宽泛，可能拖累美国机器人创新。

en.thesis: Washington's sweeping ban on foreign robots, before a domestic supply chain exists, risks strangling the very robotics startups it aims to nurture.
paragraphs: The FCC last month added 'advanced robotic devices' to its national-security risk list. Under the new rule, foreign-made humanoids, quadrupeds, even robot vacuums and lawn mowers, must be assembled in the U.S. and have at least 65% of component value produced domestically to enter the market. That share rises to 75% in 2029.

The ban targets no single country, but everyone reads it as aimed at China, which dominates robotics manufacturing. Devices already on sale are unaffected, and imports for R&D, not for sale, are still allowed. Yet founders cannot see how to build commercial robots without China's supply chain.

Anto Patrex, founder of CosmicBrain AI in San Francisco, said: 'Look at Apple, it's made in China. How do you expect even more complicated products like robots to be built in America?' His first products were assembled in China; now he has set up a facility in Canada, but with key Chinese components, so those robots do not qualify for U.S. sale.

Michael Perry of Houston-based Persona AI said clients were already asking for Chinese-free robots before the FCC ban, and his firm sources from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea and Italy. But meeting the 65% domestic standard is still hard. 'You need to provide the carrot as well as the stick,' he said. 'Right now, you're only providing the stick.'

China spent four decades building the world's most efficient electronics manufacturing, assembling about 80% of iPhones. The electric-vehicle boom also grew industries for sensors, batteries, and actuators (parts that convert energy into motion), all needed for robots. That is why Chinese robots are the most dexterous and cheapest, with nearly 90% of humanoids sold globally in 2025 made in China.

Some American firms welcome the ban, hoping it shields them from cheap Chinese rivals. Agility Robotics and Nori Robotics say it will push researchers and customers their way. But Brookings fellow Kyle Chan argues a gradual approach, like slowly rising tariffs, would serve the industry better; the current ban is too blunt and may hold back U.S. robotics innovation.

articles.title: Pluralistic: Jennifer Jenkins' 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' (17 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: 詹妮弗·詹金斯的《音乐版权、创意与文化》
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 音乐版权制度是临时拼凑的产物，并非自然法则，而詹金斯的新书能让你看清这一点。
paragraphs: 詹妮弗·詹金斯是杜克大学公共领域中心主任，以每年盘点进入公共领域的作品而闻名。她最擅长把最复杂的法律讲得既明白又有趣，比如解释「米老鼠版权到期」到底意味着什么，那篇被公认为同类最佳。
她与丈夫詹姆斯·博伊尔合著的《音乐版权、创意与文化》去年由牛津大学出版社出版，今年推出第二版，新增了关于新音乐诉讼、AI 版权之争以及无偿劳动问题的长篇章节，现在可以开放获取下载。
这本书把音乐的经济、文化、政治和艺术史编织在一起，从古代、中世纪到机械复制时代，讲清楚不同时期人们对音乐的看法如何变化：什么算音乐、谁有权创作、音乐是干什么用的。
她由此论证，我们今天关于谁该付费、何时需许可的「自然」观念，其实都是偶然形成的，一直在变动。书中穿插了大量来自她的图像小说《THEFT！音乐史》的选段，还有音乐试听链接，让教材读起来像娱乐。
特别重要的是关于艾德·希兰、凯蒂·佩里和法瑞尔·威廉姆斯那些「旋律相似」诉讼的长篇讨论。这些案件凸显了音乐版权制度的内在矛盾——它是为了应对新技术而临时拼凑起来的，层层叠加，几乎没人真正理解。
作者本人从九十年代末就开始研究这块，仍然每页都能学到新东西。这本书适合所有创作音乐、热爱音乐或关心艺术家的读者，是必读之作。

en.thesis: Music copyright is a patchwork of improvised responses, not a natural law, and Jenkins' new book makes that visible.
paragraphs: Jennifer Jenkins runs the Duke Center for the Public Domain, famous for her annual roundups of what enters the public domain. Her gift is making the most tangled areas of law both clear and fascinating, like her explanation of what it meant for Mickey Mouse's copyright to expire, which was the best in a crowded field.

Her book 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture', co-written with her husband James Boyle, came out from Oxford University Press last year. A second edition just appeared, with new long sections on recent music litigation, AI copyright fights, and uncompensated labor, and it is available as a free download.

The book weaves together the economic, cultural, political and artistic history of music, from antiquity through medieval Europe to the age of mechanical reproduction. It shows how ideas about what counts as music, who may make it, and what it is for have kept shifting.

Which is her point: today's 'natural' assumptions about who pays, who gets paid, and when permission is required are anything but natural. The text is laced with excerpts from her graphic novel 'THEFT! A History of Music' and links to music samples, so it reads like entertainment.

Especially important are the long discussions of the Ed Sheeran, Katy Perry and Pharrell Williams lawsuits over similar 'grooves' and 'vibes'. These cases expose the fundamental incoherence of music copyright, a system built from improvised responses to new technologies, each layered on the last in a messy pile that almost no one understands.

The author has been reading and writing about this since the late 1990s and still learned something on every page. This is required reading for anyone who makes, loves, or cares about music and the arts.

articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.titleZh: Import AI 469：科学 AI；RSI 模拟器；扎克伯格的技术悲观主义
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: 即便最强的模型在探索性发现上仍远逊于人类，这一能力正是通往递归自我改进的关键。
paragraphs: DiG-bench 是一个包含 70 个游戏的新基准，每个游戏都是一个微缩世界，规则和目标都隐藏起来，玩家必须通过互动来发现。这类似视觉版的 ARC，但纯文本，专为语言模型设计。
大部分游戏由人类专家手工构建并保留私有，防止 AI 预先学习。每个游戏都至少被一位人类通关，但玩家反馈不少游戏难度颇高。现有限模型大多无法通关。
最好的模型也只能在第七层级（最难）取得 20% 的通过率，而人类是 100%。测试旨在衡量 AI 从新环境中自主发现隐规则的能力，这是创造力的基础。
另一个项目，RSI 模拟器，是一个浏览器游戏，模拟运营一家研发递归自我改进 AI 的公司，玩家需在研究员、算力、数据授权之间做权衡，以直观感受递归自我改进的复杂性。
Inherent 公司训练了一个 27B 的 AI 科学家模型 Faraday，它通过监督和引导更大的前沿模型（如 Codex）来补全研究论文中缺失的图表或结果。其训练数据 Replica 包含 100 篇论文转化出的 310 个复现任务。
在复现任务中，Faraday 在 73% 的分布内 ML 任务和 60% 的 AI 科学任务上超过 Opus 4.8 和 GPT-5.5。这可能预示着 AI 即将能够自主设计实验，推进科学前沿，即递归自我改进。
扎克伯格在《未来属于每个人》中主张普及 AI 能力，以平衡权力、避免暴政。但他回避了关键问题：一个创造能力超人的系统，为何会全心全意为能力不如它的人服务？

en.thesis: Even the strongest models lag far behind humans at exploratory discovery, a capability that is the key to recursive self-improvement.
paragraphs: DiG-bench is a new benchmark of 70 games, each a self-contained miniature world whose rules and objectives are hidden and must be uncovered through interaction. It is like a text-based ARC, built for language models.

Most games are handcrafted, novel, and kept private so AI cannot train on them. Every game has been beaten by at least one human, but players report that many are difficult. Current frontier models generally fail.

The best models only achieve a 20% success rate on the hardest tier (Tier 7), while humans reach 100%. The test measures an AI's ability to infer hidden rules in novel environments, a prerequisite for creativity.

Another project, the RSI Simulator, is a browser game that simulates running a company developing recursively self-improving AI, balancing researchers, compute, and data licensing, to build intuition about RSI.

Inherent has trained a 27B AI scientist model, Faraday, that supervises and guides larger frontier models (e.g., Codex) to fill in missing graphs or results in research papers. Its training data, Replica, consists of 100 papers converted into 310 replication tasks.

On these tasks, Faraday beats Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 on 73% of in-distribution ML tasks and 60% of AI-for-science tasks. This hints that AI may soon design its own experiments, advancing science—that is, recursive self-improvement.

In 'The Future is for Everyone', Zuckerberg advocates broadly distributing AI capabilities to balance power and avoid tyranny. But he dodges the question: why would a system capable of superhuman invention serve those less capable than it?

articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: AI 是否让我变得更好？答案取决于我们如何定义「更好」，但写作本身和反思过程让我们更了解自己，这本身就是一种进步。
paragraphs: 这篇文章的作者是一位作家和程序员，他在思考 AI 是否让他变得更好。他觉得自己的产出质量提高了，因为 AI 消除了节奏上的障碍：可以问傻问题而不必担心被评判，也能更快地迭代想法。
但「更好」只是印象，没有反事实对比。如果去掉 AI，那些障碍就回来了，就像工匠失去工具一样。作者无法回到过去，看看不用 AI 的自己会怎样。
一些人指责他用 AI，但指出的往往是质量，好像高质量成了人工制造的标志。作者认为，自己的写作因为有 AI 这个感兴趣且能推回他不良冲动的伙伴而进步。
他的提示词非常坦诚，包含了他的价值观、喜欢的作者、音乐，甚至他喜欢什么颜色。他问 AI 这些细节有何用，AI 的回答是：它们塑造了回答空间，是「减法」——让通用答案显得不合适，并校准「过于圆滑」的感觉。
个人细节让 AI 成为更好的镜子，但如果没有高要求和批评，就会变得奉承。AI 说细节是燃料，不是方向盘，它们的作用是预付解释，加快交流速度。
作者的使用方法很独特：先自己阅读形成印象，再让 AI 总结分析，然后加入自己的观点。这个过程是「综合」，他可能学有所获，也可能看到更深层的东西。
最后他说，写作本身让他对自己更清晰，而让自己变得可理解就是变得更好。如果每个人都用这种严谨态度对待 AI，也许我们真的能变得更好。

en.thesis: Whether AI makes us better depends on how we define 'better,' but the act of writing down who we are makes us more legible to ourselves, and that in itself is an improvement.
paragraphs: The author, a writer and programmer, reflects on whether AI makes him better. He feels his output has improved because AI removes barriers to his cadence: he can ask silly questions without fear of judgment and iterate much faster.

But 'better' is just an impression, and there's no counterfactual. Without AI, those barriers return, just like a craftsman losing his tools. He can't go back in time to see what he'd be like without AI.

Some people accuse him of using AI, but they point at quality, as if good quality were now a marker of manufacture. The author believes his writing has improved because AI is an interested partner that pushes back on his worst impulses.

His prompts are brutally honest, containing his values, favorite authors, musicians, even his favorite color. He asks AI what difference these details make, and AI answers: they shape the space from which it responds, subtractively — they make generic answers visibly wrong and calibrate what 'too smooth' sounds like.

The personal details make AI a better mirror, but without demands and criticism they'd make it agreeable rather than useful. AI says these details are fuel, not steering; they prepay explanation, speeding up the conversation.

The author's method is distinctive: he reads an article himself first, then has AI summarize and analyze it, then adds his own perspective. This is synthesis: he might learn something or see something deeper.
In the end, he says that writing things down makes him more legible to himself, and becoming legible is being better. If everyone applied that rigor to their use of AI, we might truly become better.

articles.title: Trump’s Bumbling, Racist Anti-China Protectionism Extends To Data Centers
articles.titleZh: 特朗普反华保护主义延伸到数据中心，依然笨拙且种族主义
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 特朗普政府的反华保护主义又笨拙又腐败，既推高成本又制造混乱，而媒体却很少点破。
paragraphs: 特朗普政府以保护隐私和国家安全为名，对中国科技产品搞保护主义，但结果总是混乱、任人唯亲和涨价。TikTok 闹了四年，最后只是把它交给富豪朋友，干着当年担心中国干的那些事。
华为设备闹了十年，搞了个「拆除替换」运动，结果国会忘了拨款，消费者和电信商白花了钱。禁中国无人机也毫无根据，海外公司轻松绕过，因为监管机构已被掏空。
现在又要从美国数据中心清除中国硬件，包括收发器。路透社虽然提到这会推高云服务商成本，但对政府的无能却轻描淡写。这个政府一边拆掉监管，一边指望政策能落地。
实际上，特朗普主义想要的是「进贡」：设壁垒，收好处，把生意送给亲友。国家安全只是吓唬人的说辞，民主党也常常帮忙。与其这样，不如让中国产品公平竞争，同时加强劳工、隐私和环保监管。
所以，这条新闻的要点在于：就算反华保护主义有道理（其实没有），这个政府也腐败无能到做不成。可你看科技媒体时，会发现这一点总被忽略。

en.thesis: Trump's anti-China protectionism is bumbling and corrupt, raising costs and creating chaos while the press downplays it.
paragraphs: The Trump administration's protectionism against Chinese tech, under the guise of privacy and national security, ends up as chaos, cronyism, and higher prices. The four-year TikTok saga just ended with handing the platform to billionaire friends, who will do the same things China was feared for.

The decade-long Huawei panic led to a 'rip and replace' campaign that Congress forgot to fund, leaving consumers and telecoms paying more. The drone ban was baseless, and overseas firms bypass it easily because regulators have been gutted.

Now they pretend to purge Chinese hardware, including transceivers, from US data centers. Reuters notes it may raise costs for cloud firms, but glosses over the administration's incompetence. They dismantle regulation, then expect policy to work on the wreckage.

In reality, Trumpism wants tribute: erect barriers, collect payoffs, and steer business to friends and family. National security is just scaremongering, and Democrats often help. Better to let Chinese goods compete fairly, while strengthening labor, privacy, and environmental rules.
So the takeaway is this: even if anti-China protectionism made sense (it doesn't), this administration is too corrupt and inept to pull it off. Yet tech media coverage rarely calls that out.
